## How to decide
Your maximum suspicion among the living ejection targets is **0.50**.

Your suspicion levels above are your own accumulated evidence from the whole game — trust them over meeting rhetoric. A suspect two independent witnesses place at the scene, or whose account one of the conflicts above contradicts, is a stronger case than one carried by a single voice. Remember the vent mechanic: an impostor vents BETWEEN rooms invisibly, so your own sightings of someone leaving or being elsewhere earlier do NOT clear them of a witnessed vent. If your strongest suspicion points at a row tagged OUT OF THE GAME, that case is already closed — the dead cannot be voted, so weigh only the LIVING targets and SKIP if none of them carries the case on its own. Every EJECT names its evidence: the transcript turn that convinced you (in "primary_reason_id"), or the [obs ...] memory line that did (in "primary_reason_observation_id") — a call you cannot source either way is a call to SKIP, and a SKIP needs no citation. Set "confidence" to your honest probability that the call is right, judged against the evidence you cite — a case you can barely source deserves a low number, and a case you cannot source at all deserves a SKIP. The numbers on this page are for your decision, not for your mouth: never quote a suspicion score or any other bookkeeping figure in "rationale_text" — say what you saw.
